extracted.intended_audience: individuals and organizations (and their counsel) submitting citizen petitions, petitions for stay, petitions for reconsideration, or participating in FDA rulemaking and notice-and-comment proceedings; FDA docket staff and practitioners in administrative law
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for submitting and evaluating citizen petitions, petitions for stay, petitions for reconsideration, and for notice-and-comment rulemaking under FDA authority (21 CFR part 10). Covers record composition, timing, form, and standards the Commissioner uses to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mootness and dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: If changes in law, facts, or circumstances since the petition was submitted have rendered the petition moot, the Commissioner may dismiss the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner is to be notified of the Commissioner's decision. The decision will be placed in the public docket file and may also be in the form of a notice published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeframe for petitions under section 505(j)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall furnish a response to each petitioner within 90 days of receipt of a petition filed under section 505(j)(2)(C) of the act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response will either approve or disapprove the petition. Agency action on a petition shall be governed by § 314.93 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeframe for petitions subject to section 505(q)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner intends to furnish a response to each petitioner within 150 days of receipt of a petition subject to section 505(q) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of rulemaking provisions when petition requests regulatory relief
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition filed under paragraph (c) of this section requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, § 10.40 or § 10.50 also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing, amending, and withdrawing petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may supplement, amend, or withdraw a petition without Agency approval and without prejudice to resubmission at any time until the Commissioner rules on the petition, unless the petition has been referred for a hearing under parts 12, 13, 14, or 15. After a ruling or referral, a petition may be supplemented, amended, or withdrawn only with the approval of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may approve withdrawal, with or without prejudice against resubmission of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures Commissioner may use in reviewing a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: In reviewing a petition the Commissioner may use conferences/meetings/correspondence (§ 10.65), hearings (parts 12–16), Federal Register notices requesting information and views, proposals to issue/amend/revoke regulations (§ 10.40 or § 12.20), or any other specific public procedure established in this chapter and expressly applicable to the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the administrative record for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the administrative proceeding consists of (1) the petition, including all information on which it relies, filed by the Dockets Management Staff; (2) all comments received on the petition, including all information submitted as a part of the comments; (3) if petition resulted in a proposal to issue/amend/revoke a regulation, all documents specified in § 10.40(g); (4) the record of optional procedures (transcripts, minutes, reports, FR notices, etc.) except transcripts of closed portion of public advisory committee meetings; (5) the Commissioner's decision and supporting information filed with the Dockets Management Staff; (6) all documents filed under § 10.65(h); (7) if a petition for reconsideration or for a stay is filed, the administrative record specified in § 10.33(k) or § 10.35(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items together form the administrative record supporting the Commissioner's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity and closing of the administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative record specified is the exclusive record for the Commissioner's decision. The record of the administrative proceeding closes on the date of the Commissioner's decision unless some other date is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thereafter any interested person may submit a petition for reconsideration under § 10.33 or a petition for stay under § 10.35. A person who wishes to rely upon information or views not included in the administrative record shall submit them to the Commissioner with a new petition to modify the decision in accordance with this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: routine correspondence and law-enforcement referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to the referral of a matter to a United States attorney for the initiation of court enforcement action and related correspondence, or to requests, suggestions, and recommendations made informally in routine correspondence received by FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine correspondence does not constitute a petition within the meaning of this section unless it purports to meet the requirements of this section. Action on routine correspondence does not constitute final administrative action subject to judicial review under § 10.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dockets Management Staff listing of petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dockets Management Staff will maintain a chronological list of each petition filed under this section and § 10.85, showing (1) the docket number; (2) the date the petition was filed by the Dockets Management Staff; (3) the name of the petitioner; (4) the subject matter involved; and (5) the disposition of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list excludes petitions submitted elsewhere in the agency under § 10.25(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of § 10.31 to certain drug/biologic-related petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: § 10.31 applies to a citizen petition or petition for stay of action that meets all of the following: (1) requests action that could delay approval of an ANDA under 505(j), a new drug application under 505(b)(2), or a biologics license application under 351(k); (2) is submitted on or after Sept 27, 2007; (3) is submitted in writing and under § 10.30 (for citizen petitions) or § 10.35 (for petitions for stay of action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of submission is date received by Dockets Management Staff
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition subject to § 10.31 and submitted in accordance with applicable sections is regarded as submitted on the date on which the petition is received by the Dockets Management Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirements for § 10.31 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not consider for review a petition that is subject to § 10.31 unless the petition is in writing and contains the required certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must contain one or more specific dates (month, day, year) in the first blank space provided. If different categories of information become known at different times, the certification must contain each estimated relevant date. The information associated with a particular date must be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification for supplemental information/comments under § 10.31
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not accept for review any supplemental information or comments on a petition subject to § 10.31 unless the supplemental information or comments are in writing and contain the required verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The verification must contain one or more specific dates (month, day, year) in the first blank space provided. If different categories of information become known at different times, the verification must contain each estimated relevant date. The information associated with a particular date must be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's authority to reconsider matters (§ 10.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may at any time reconsider a matter, on the Commissioner's own initiative or on the petition of an interested person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for petitions for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may request reconsideration of part or all of a decision of the Commissioner on a petition submitted under § 10.25. Each request must be submitted in accordance with § 10.20 and in the specified form no later than 30 days after the date of the decision involved. The petition must include: (A) Decision involved (concise statement); (B) Action requested (what petitioner requests); (C) Statement of grounds (a full statement, well-organized, of factual and legal grounds demonstrating that relevant information and views contained in the administrative record were not previously or adequately considered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new information or views may be included in a petition for reconsideration. The Commissioner may, for good cause, permit a petition to be filed after 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for granting reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may grant a petition for reconsideration when the Commissioner determines it is in the public interest and in the interest of justice. The Commissioner shall grant a petition for reconsideration in any proceeding if all of the following apply: (1) petition demonstrates that relevant information or views contained in the administrative record were not previously or not adequately considered; (2) petitioner's position is not frivolous and is being pursued in good faith; (3) petitioner has demonstrated sound public policy grounds supporting reconsideration; (4) reconsideration is not outweighed by public health or other public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and preclusion of new information in reconsideration petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for reconsideration may not be based on information and views not contained in the administrative record on which the decision was made. An interested person who wishes to rely on information or views not included in the administrative record shall submit them with a new petition to modify the decision under § 10.25(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner shall promptly review a petition for reconsideration. A petition submitted later than 30 days after the date of the decision will be denied as untimely unless the Commissioner permits the petition to be filed after 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration decisions and public display
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on a petition for reconsideration is to be in writing and placed on public display as part of the docket file on the matter. A determination to grant reconsideration will be published in the Federal Register if the Commissioner's original decision was so published. Any other determination to grant or deny reconsideration may also be published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of the administrative proceeding for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The record consists of: (1) the record of the original petition specified in § 10.30(i); (2) the petition for reconsideration, including all information on which it relies; (3) all comments received on the petition; (4) the Commissioner's decision on the petition under paragraph (f) including supporting information filed with Dockets; (5) any Federal Register notices or other documents resulting; (6) all documents filed under § 10.65(h); (7) if the Commissioner reconsiders the matter, the administrative record relating to reconsideration specified in § 10.30(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's authority to stay or extend effective dates (§ 10.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may at any time stay or extend the effective date of an action pending or following a decision on any matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a stay of action – form, timing, and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may request the Commissioner to stay the effective date of any administrative action. A stay may be requested for a specific time period or for an indefinite time period. A request for stay must be submitted in accordance with § 10.20 and in the specified form no later than 30 days after the date of the decision involved (Commissioner may, for good cause, permit a petition after 30 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For petitions subject to § 10.31, the request must also include the § 10.31 certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay does not automatically suspend action — grounds for staying
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the filing of a petition for a stay of action nor action taken by an interested person in accordance with any other administrative procedure will stay or otherwise delay any administrative action by the Commissioner, including enforcement action of any kind, unless one of the following applies: (1) Commissioner determines that a stay or delay is in the public interest and stays the action; (2) a statute requires the matter be stayed; (3) a court orders that the matter be stayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for granting a stay of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall promptly review a petition for stay of action and may grant or deny a petition, in whole or in part. The Commissioner may grant a stay in any proceeding if it is in the public interest and in the interest of justice. The Commissioner shall grant a stay in any proceeding if all of the following apply: (1) The petitioner will otherwise suffer irreparable injury; (2) The petitioner's case is not frivolous and is being pursued in good faith; (3) The petitioner has demonstrated sound public policy grounds supporting the stay; (4) The delay resulting from the stay is not outweighed by public health or other public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of stay decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner's decision on a petition for stay of action is to be in writing and placed on public display as part of the file on the matter in the office of the Dockets Management Staff. A determination to grant a stay will be published in the Federal Register if the Commissioner's original decision was so published. Any other determination to grant or to deny a stay may also be published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness rules for petitions for stay
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for a stay of action submitted later than 30 days after the date of the decision involved will be denied as untimely unless the Commissioner permits the petition to be filed after 30 days. A petition for a stay of action is considered submitted on the day it is received by the Dockets Management Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record composition for stay proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the administrative proceeding for a stay consists of: (1) the record of the proceeding to which the petition for stay is directed; (2) the petition for stay of action, including all information on which it relies; (3) all comments received on the petition, including all information submitted as part of the comments; (4) the Commissioner's decision on the petition under paragraph (e) including supporting information filed with the Dockets; (5) any Federal Register notices or other documents resulting from the petition; (6) all documents filed under § 10.65(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing/amending/withdrawing petitions for stay
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may supplement, amend, or withdraw a petition for stay of action in writing without Agency approval and without prejudice to resubmission at any time until the Commissioner rules on the petition, provided the resubmission is made in accordance with paragraph (b), unless the petition has been referred for a hearing under parts 12–15. After a ruling or referral, a petition for stay of action may be supplemented, amended, or withdrawn only with the approval of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may approve withdrawal with or without prejudice against resubmission of the petition for stay of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's authority to propose and promulgate regulations (§ 10.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may propose and promulgate regulations for the efficient enforcement of the laws administered by FDA whenever it is necessary or appropriate to do so. The issuance, amendment, or revocation of a regulation may be initiated in any of the ways specified in § 10.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for publishing an interested person's proposed regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulation proposed by an interested person in a petition submitted under § 10.25(a) will be published in the Federal Register as a proposal if: (i) the petition contains facts demonstrating reasonable grounds for the proposal; and (ii) the petition substantially shows that the proposal is in the public interest and will promote the objectives of the act and the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing multiple alternatives and Commissioner's preliminary views
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more alternative proposed regulations may be published on the same subject to obtain comment on the different alternatives. A regulation proposed by an interested person may be published together with the Commissioner's preliminary views on the proposal and any alternative proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a notice of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (e), each regulation must be the subject of a notice of proposed rulemaking published in the Federal Register. The notice will contain: (i) the name of the agency; (ii) the nature of the action; (iii) a summary first paragraph describing the substance in easily understandable terms; (iv) relevant dates; (v) name, business address, and phone number of an agency contact; (vi) an address for submitting written comments; (vii) supplementary information in a preamble summarizing the proposal and facts/policy underlying it and references to all information on which the Commissioner relies; (viii) either the terms/substance of the proposed regulation or a description of subjects/issues involved; (ix) a reference to existence or lack of need for an environmental impact statement under § 25.52; (x) the docket number of the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble must include references to all information on which the Commissioner relies (copies or list are part of docket file) and cite authority under which regulation is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of comment period for proposed regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal will provide 60 days for comment, although the Commissioner may shorten or lengthen this time period for good cause. In no event is the time for comment to be less than 10 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication of the proposed rule, any interested person may request the Commissioner to extend the comment period for an additional specified period by submitting a written request to the Dockets Management Staff stating the grounds for the request, headed 'REQUEST FOR EXTENSION OF COMMENT PERIOD.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request must discuss why comments could not feasibly be submitted within the time permitted, or that important new information will shortly be available, or that sound public policy supports an extension. Commissioner may grant/deny or grant a different extension. An extension of 30 days or longer will be published in the Federal Register and apply to all interested persons; an extension of less than 30 days will be the subject either of a letter or memorandum filed with the Dockets Management Staff or of a notice published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission format and docketing
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of proposed rulemaking will request that four copies of all comments be submitted to the Dockets Management Staff, except that individuals may submit single copies. Comments will be stamped with the date of receipt and will be numbered chronologically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to propose alternative wording when criticizing a proposed regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons submitting comments critical of a proposed regulation are encouraged to include their preferred alternative wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-comment decisionmaking process for proposed regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: After the time for comment on a proposed regulation has expired, the Commissioner will review the entire administrative record on the matter and, in a notice published in the Federal Register, will terminate the proceeding, issue a new proposal, or promulgate a final regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of decision on proposed regulation — quality and administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality and persuasiveness of the comments will be the basis for the Commissioner's decision. The number or length of comments will not ordinarily be a significant factor in the decision unless the number of comments is material where the degree of public interest is a legitimate factor for consideration. The decision of the Commissioner on the matter will be based solely upon the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final regulation preamble content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A final regulation published in the Federal Register will have a preamble stating: (i) the name of the agency, (ii) the nature of the action, (iii) a summary first paragraph describing the substance, (iv) relevant dates, (v) the name, business address, and phone number of an agency contact, (vi) an address for submission of written comments when permitted, (vii) supplementary information in the body of the preamble that contains references to prior notices and a summary of each type of comment submitted on the proposal and the Commissioner's conclusions with respect to each. The preamble is to contain a thorough and comprehensible explanation of the reasons for the Commissioner's decision on each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date minimum and exceptions for final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective date of a final regulation may not be less than 30 days after the date of publication in the Federal Register, except for: (i) a regulation that grants an exemption or relieves a restriction; or (ii) a regulation for which the Commissioner finds, and states in the notice, good cause for an earlier effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of APA notice-and-comment and Commissioner's discretionary use
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions for notice and comment in paragraphs (b) and (c) apply only to the extent required by the Administrative Procedure Act (5 U.S.C. 551, 552, and 553). As a matter of discretion, the Commissioner may voluntarily follow those provisions in circumstances in which they are not required by the APA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to notice and comment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of notice and public procedure do not apply in the following situations: (1) When the Commissioner determines for good cause that they are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest (in which case the notice will state reasons and provide an opportunity for comment to determine whether the regulation should subsequently be modified or revoked); (2) food additive and color additive petitions subject to § 12.20(b)(2); (3) new animal drug regulations promulgated under section 512(i) of the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional public procedures available for proposed or final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to notice and public procedure, the Commissioner may subject a proposed or final regulation to additional procedures including: (1) conferences/meetings/ correspondence (§ 10.65), (2) hearings under parts 12–15, (3) a Federal Register notice requesting information and views before determining whether to propose a regulation, (4) a draft of a proposed regulation placed on public display in the office of the Dockets Management Staff, (5) a revised proposal published in the Federal Register, (6) a tentative final regulation or tentative revised final regulation placed on public display (and possibly published), (7) a final regulation published that provides an opportunity for submission of further comments, (8) any other public procedure expressly applicable to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drafts or tentative documents are placed on display only, the Commissioner shall publish an appropriate notice stating availability and time for comments; mailing may be required to commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative record composition for regulation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the administrative proceeding for a regulation consists of: (1) if initiated by a petition, the administrative record specified in § 10.30(i); (2) if a petition for reconsideration or stay is filed, the records in §§ 10.33(k) and 10.35(h); (3) the proposed rule published in the Federal Register including all information identified or filed by the Commissioner on the proposal; (4) all comments received on the proposal; (5) the notice promulgating the final regulation including all information identified or filed by the Commissioner with the Dockets as part of the administrative record of the final regulation; (6) transcripts, minutes, reports, FR notices, and other documents resulting from the additional procedures, but not closed advisory committee transcripts; (7) all documents submitted under § 10.65(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record closing and post-final remedies for regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the administrative proceeding closes on the date of publication of the final regulation in the Federal Register unless some other date is specified. Thereafter, any interested person may submit a petition for reconsideration under § 10.33 or a petition for stay of action under § 10.35. A person who wishes to rely on information or views not included in the administrative record shall submit it to the Commissioner with a new petition to modify the final regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dockets Management Staff list of regulations proposed and promulgated
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dockets Management Staff shall maintain a chronological list of all regulations proposed and promulgated under this section and § 10.50 showing (1) the docket number (and center designation where applicable), (2) the name of the petitioner, if any, (3) the subject matter involved, and (4) the disposition of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of administrative remedies before judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: A request that the Commissioner take or refrain from taking any form of administrative action must first be the subject of a final administrative decision based on a petition submitted under § 10.25(a) or, where applicable, a hearing under § 16.1(b) before any legal action is filed in a court complaining of the action or failure to act. If a court action is filed before the submission of the decision, the Commissioner shall request dismissal or referral to the agency for initial administrative determination on grounds of failure to exhaust administrative remedies, lack of final agency action, and lack of an actual controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to seek administrative stay before judicial stay
rubrics_metrics.description: A request that administrative action be stayed must first be the subject of an administrative decision based upon a petition for stay of action submitted under § 10.35 before a request is made that a court stay the action. If a court action is filed requesting a stay before the Commissioner's decision on a timely petition, the Commissioner shall request dismissal or referral to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final agency action ripeness and availability of judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, the Commissioner's final decision constitutes final agency action (reviewable in the courts under 5 U.S.C. 701 et seq., and, where appropriate, 28 U.S.C. 2201) on petitions submitted under § 10.25(a), petitions for reconsideration under § 10.33, petitions for stay under § 10.35, advisory opinions under § 10.85, matters involving hearings under § 16.1(b), or issuance of a final regulation published in accordance with § 10.40, except where statutes provide otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is FDA's position that final agency action exhausts administrative remedies and is ripe for preenforcement judicial review as of the date of the final decision, unless applicable law explicitly requires further action before judicial review is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's objections to judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall object to judicial review of a matter if: (i) the matter is committed by law to the discretion of the Commissioner (e.g., enforcement decisions); or (ii) review is not sought in a proper court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative record as sole basis for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall take the position in actions for judicial review that the validity of the action must be determined solely on the basis of the administrative record specified in §§ 10.30(i), 10.33(k), 10.35(h), 10.40(g), and 16.80(a) (or the applicable administrative record for hearings), and that additional information or views may not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interested person who wishes to rely upon information or views not included in the administrative record shall submit them to the Commissioner with a new petition to modify the action under § 10.25(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's approach to multiple judicial filings (multiplicity of suits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner requests that all petitions for judicial review of a particular matter be filed in a single U.S. District court. If petitions are filed in more than one jurisdiction, the Commissioner will take appropriate action to prevent multiplicity of suits such as requesting transfer, staying other actions, requesting dismissal of other actions pending conclusion of one proceeding, or requesting one suit be maintained as a class action on behalf of all affected persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Court of Appeals petitions under 28 U.S.C. 2112(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of 28 U.S.C. 2112(a), a copy of any petition filed in any U.S. Court of Appeals challenging a final action of the Commissioner shall be sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by personal delivery to the Chief Counsel of FDA. The petition copy shall be time-stamped by the clerk of the court when the original is filed. The Chief Counsel requests that the purpose of all petitions mailed or delivered to the Office of Chief Counsel to satisfy 28 U.S.C. 2112(a) be clearly identified in a cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of receipt date for 28 U.S.C. 2112(a) petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Chief Counsel receives two or more petitions filed in two or more U.S. Courts of Appeals for review of any agency action within 10 days of the effective date of that action, the Chief Counsel will notify the U.S. Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation. For the purpose of determining whether a petition for review has been received within the 10-day period, the petition shall be considered to be received on the date of delivery if personally delivered.
